_readme: Measured examples only; see _meta and ui/content/README.md.

_meta.purpose: Measured, curated examples. Failure cases are DELIBERATELY the hardest validation windows for the attention model and do not represent average performance. Neither model reports uncertainty or calibrated confidence.
_meta.split: validation (the test split is not used)
_meta.corpus: local ZIPs verified against docs/jena-mpi-roof-checksums.txt; Supabase was not contacted
_meta.run_id_note: run ids are as reported by the user for the registered runs; not verified by this script

comparison_examples.title: Strong daily cycle: both models follow the shape and overshoot the afternoon peak
comparison_examples.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2020-04-07T00:00:00): last observed 9.78 °C; actual next 24 h ranged 4.37 to 17.38 °C (mean 12.11). LSTM run 1: MAE 1.11 °C, mean signed error +0.85 °C, forecast range 4.83 to 20.92 °C. Attention run 4: MAE 1.01 °C, mean signed error +0.77 °C, forecast range 5.38 to 20.28 °C. Persistence (repeat the last value) MAE for reference: 4.69 °C.

Observation: the previous day rose from about 1 °C to 21.8 °C; the next day actually peaked at 17.4 °C. Both forecasts have the right overnight low and morning rise, but peak too high (LSTM 20.9 °C, attention 20.3 °C), close to the previous day's peak rather than the actual one, so most of each model's error is the afternoon overshoot of roughly 3 to 4 °C. Both are far better than persistence on this window. Speculation (not tested): the models may be reproducing the amplitude of the day just seen; a univariate temperature history carries no information about the cloud or air-mass change that held the actual peak down. This is one window and says nothing about which model is better overall.

comparison_examples.title: Nearly constant temperature: small errors, and persistence is competitive
comparison_examples.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2020-10-17T00:00:00): last observed 7.01 °C; actual next 24 h ranged 6.66 to 7.90 °C (mean 7.31). LSTM run 1: MAE 0.63 °C, mean signed error -0.54 °C, forecast range 5.64 to 7.31 °C. Attention run 4: MAE 0.41 °C, mean signed error -0.21 °C, forecast range 6.12 to 7.74 °C. Persistence (repeat the last value) MAE for reference: 0.44 °C.

Observation: the whole 96 hours stayed within about 4 °C. Persistence has MAE 0.44 °C, the attention model 0.41 °C and the LSTM 0.63 °C, so on this window the LSTM is worse than just repeating the last value and the attention model is about equal to it. Both forecasts drift downward over the last hours (to 6.1 °C and 5.6 °C) while the actual temperature stayed near 7.4 °C. Speculation (not tested): the downward drift may reflect an evening-cooling pattern learned from other days. Calm windows like this are where a forecast adds the least over the trivial baseline.

comparison_examples.title: Large level change: both models miss most of a 20 °C afternoon
comparison_examples.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2021-03-29T00:00:00): last observed 9.58 °C; actual next 24 h ranged 7.63 to 20.13 °C (mean 13.26). LSTM run 1: MAE 3.74 °C, mean signed error -3.66 °C, forecast range 7.38 to 12.24 °C. Attention run 4: MAE 2.93 °C, mean signed error -2.92 °C, forecast range 7.48 to 13.79 °C. Persistence (repeat the last value) MAE for reference: 4.41 °C.

Observation: the preceding day peaked at 12.2 °C and the actual next day reached 20.1 °C. Both forecasts show a smaller daytime rise (attention peaks at 13.8 °C, LSTM at 12.2 °C), about 6 to 8 °C below the actual afternoon values. The LSTM's peak equals the previous day's peak. Here the attention model has the lower MAE (2.93 versus 3.74 °C); on the validation split as a whole the LSTM's MAE is lower (1.83 versus 1.92 °C), so this window is not representative of the ranking. Speculation (not tested): a warm air mass arriving is not visible in 72 hours of temperature alone.

failure_cases.title: Failure 1 (2020-05-11): forecast daytime warming, but it kept cooling
failure_cases.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2020-05-11T03:00:00): last observed 13.77 °C; actual next 24 h ranged -0.47 to 11.63 °C. Attention run 4 forecast 12.10 to 19.00 °C: MAE 11.28 °C, mean signed error +11.28 °C, largest hourly error 16.16 °C at +11 h. The LSTM (run 1) on the same window: MAE 10.18 °C; persistence: 9.69 °C. Encoder attention: the final-hour row puts 0.77 of its weight on the last 24 input hours (max single weight 0.139); mean row entropy 2.57 nats versus 4.28 for uniform.

Observation: the window starts at 03:00. The history had already been cooling for about 12 hours (22.3 °C down to 13.8 °C). The attention forecast started at 13.3 °C, then rose to 19.0 °C about 11 hours ahead, as in a normal daily cycle. The actual temperature fell almost steadily to about 4 °C within 6 hours and reached -0.5 °C at +24 h, so the largest hourly error is 16.2 °C. The LSTM forecast a similar rise (peak 17.0 °C) and has MAE 10.18 °C; persistence has 9.69 °C, so neither model beat repeating the last value here. Attention weights are in the heatmap: the final-hour row places 0.77 of its weight on the last 24 input hours with no single weight above 0.14. Speculation (not tested): a cold-air outbreak is not visible in the preceding temperatures, and the models may be falling back on the typical daily cycle. The attention pattern is not evidence for or against that, and it is not an explanation of the error.

What this case shows: a large error from a model that displays no uncertainty. The model has no calibrated confidence, and neither the deterministic forecast nor the concentration of attention weights should be read as confidence. This case was selected because the attention model's error was large; it does not represent average performance.

failure_cases.title: Failure 2 (2021-12-24): forecast stayed near 7 to 8 °C while the temperature fell below zero
failure_cases.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2021-12-24T19:00:00): last observed 8.11 °C; actual next 24 h ranged -6.61 to 2.50 °C. Attention run 4 forecast 6.18 to 8.18 °C: MAE 10.10 °C, mean signed error +10.10 °C, largest hourly error 12.79 °C at +24 h. The LSTM (run 1) on the same window: MAE 10.04 °C; persistence: 10.81 °C. Encoder attention: the final-hour row puts 0.94 of its weight on the last 24 input hours (max single weight 0.203); mean row entropy 2.87 nats versus 4.28 for uniform.

Observation: the history had risen from about -3 °C to 9 °C and was at 8.1 °C at the origin. The attention forecast stayed between 8.2 and 6.2 °C for the whole day, essentially close to the last value. The actual temperature fell from 2.5 °C at +1 h to -6.6 °C at +24 h; the largest hourly error is 12.8 °C, at +24 h, and the first hour is already 5.6 °C off. The LSTM has MAE 10.04 °C and persistence 10.81 °C, so all three behave alike here. In the heatmap, the final-hour row puts 0.94 of its weight on the last 24 input hours (maximum single weight 0.20). Speculation (not tested): a rapid cooling that begins right after the window's last observation cannot be anticipated from temperature history alone. The attention pattern does not explain the error.

What this case shows: a large error from a model that displays no uncertainty. The model has no calibrated confidence, and neither the deterministic forecast nor the concentration of attention weights should be read as confidence. This case was selected because the attention model's error was large; it does not represent average performance.

failure_cases.title: Failure 3 (2021-04-11): forecast a return to about 17 °C after the temperature dropped to near 1 °C
failure_cases.discussion:
Measured (validation window, origin 2021-04-11T17:00:00): last observed 17.96 °C; actual next 24 h ranged 0.80 to 15.60 °C. Attention run 4 forecast 9.87 to 17.04 °C: MAE 9.94 °C, mean signed error +9.94 °C, largest hourly error 12.68 °C at +20 h. The LSTM (run 1) on the same window: MAE 10.99 °C; persistence: 14.03 °C. Encoder attention: the final-hour row puts 0.93 of its weight on the last 24 input hours (max single weight 0.222); mean row entropy 2.71 nats versus 4.28 for uniform.

Observation: the history ended in a warm evening (18.0 °C at 17:00). The attention forecast fell to 9.9 °C at about +11 h and then rose back to 17.0 °C. The actual temperature fell to 0.8 °C within 8 hours, stayed between 0.8 and 3.4 °C through +17 h, and was 6.2 °C at +24 h; the largest hourly error is 12.7 °C. The LSTM forecast a rise to 20.5 °C (MAE 10.99 °C); persistence has MAE 14.03 °C, so both models did better than persistence but still missed by about 10 °C on average. In the heatmap, the final-hour row puts 0.93 of its weight on the last 24 input hours (maximum single weight 0.22), and the most attended column on average is the last input hour. Speculation (not tested): the models expect the daytime recovery that normally follows an evening drop, and a front is not visible in temperature alone. The attention pattern does not explain the error.

What this case shows: a large error from a model that displays no uncertainty. The model has no calibrated confidence, and neither the deterministic forecast nor the concentration of attention weights should be read as confidence. This case was selected because the attention model's error was large; it does not represent average performance.
